No failed routes or frozen branches constrain this target. The claim is elementary and should be proved directly, without invoking Euclid parameterization or any Jacobi/QR machinery.

<MRA_ACTION>
  <action_type>run_parallel_workers</action_type>
  <goal>
    Produce and audit a complete, self-contained natural-language proof candidate for the root theorem
    `parity-gcd-lemma`.
  </goal>

  <route>
    Direct elementary proof.

    Core architecture:
    1. Prove the local fact that the square of an even integer is 0 mod 4 and the square of an odd integer is 1 mod 4.
    2. Prove the local prime-divisibility lemma: if p is prime and p | x^2, then p | x.
    3. Parity argument:
       - If a and b are both odd, then a^2 + b^2 ≡ 2 mod 4, impossible for a square.
       - If a and b are both even, then 2 | a and 2 | b, so 2 | c^2 and hence 2 | c, contradicting gcd(a,b,c) = 1.
       - Therefore exactly one of a, b is even.
       - The same congruence then gives c^2 ≡ 1 mod 4, so c is odd.
    4. Pairwise coprimality argument:
       - Suppose some prime p divides gcd(a,b). Then p | a and p | b, so p | c^2 and hence p | c — contradiction to gcd(a,b,c)=1.
       - The same argument using c^2 − a^2 = b^2 and c^2 − b^2 = a^2 gives gcd(a,c) = 1 and gcd(b,c) = 1.
  </route>

  <constraints>
    - Do not use unproved project theorems such as `coprime-square-lemma` or `euclid-forward-derivation`.
    - Do not use Jacobi or quadratic reciprocity foundations; they are irrelevant here.
    - The prime-divisibility lemma p | x^2 ⇒ p | x must be proved locally, e.g. via Bezout, or explicitly justified by the standard prime property.
    - Computational searches are allowed only as supporting evidence, never as proof.
    - All worker outputs are candidates; no worker may mark anything PROVED.
  </constraints>

  <workers>
    <worker role="constructive">
      <task>
        Write the complete proof candidate for:
        For all positive integers a,b,c, if a^2+b^2=c^2 and gcd(a,b,c)=1,
        then exactly one of a and b is even, c is odd, and
        gcd(a,b)=gcd(a,c)=gcd(b,c)=1.

        Include all required local lemmas:
        - parity of squares modulo 4;
        - prime-divisibility lemma p | x^2 ⇒ p | x;
        - the exact use of gcd(a,b,c)=1 in the both-even case;
        - the exact use of gcd(a,b,c)=1 in each pairwise-gcd contradiction.

        Deliver the proof text as concrete mathematics, not a vague outline.
      </task>
      <deliverable>
        Complete proof candidate in natural language, with each step labeled:
        PARITY, PAIRWISE_GCD, or LOCAL_LEMMA.
      </deliverable>
    </worker>

    <worker role="counterexample_hunter">
      <task>
        Attempt to refute each clause of the theorem. For each attempted counterexample pattern, report the exact algebraic step that blocks it:

        - Pattern A: a,b both odd, gcd(a,b,c)=1.
        - Pattern B: a,b both even, gcd(a,b,c)=1.
        - Pattern C: c even while a,b have opposite parity.
        - Pattern D: some prime p divides gcd(a,b) but no prime divides all three of a,b,c.
        - Pattern E: some prime p divides gcd(a,c) but no prime divides all three.
        - Pattern F: some prime p divides gcd(b,c) but no prime divides all three.

        Optionally run a bounded search over positive integer triples
        with a,b,c ≤ 300 to confirm no counterexample exists. Label any search result strictly as COMPUTATIONAL_EVIDENCE, not proof.
      </task>
      <deliverable>
        A short counterexample-hunting report: each attempted pattern, the blocking step, and the verdict NO_COUNTEREXAMPLE under the stated assumptions.
      </deliverable>
    </worker>

    <worker role="boundary_auditor">
      <task>
        Audit the constructive proof candidate and the counterexample report for boundary correctness:

        - Check p = 2 separately from odd primes wherever needed.
        - Check the exclusive meaning of “exactly one of a and b is even”.
        - Verify that c odd is derived, not assumed.
        - Verify that gcd(a,b,c)=1 means “no prime divides all three”, and that this is used exactly in the right places.
        - Verify that positivity matters or is not silently weakened.
        - Verify no hidden reliance on c > a or c > b.
        - Verify that the prime-divisibility lemma is proved without circularity.
      </task>
      <deliverable>
        Boundary audit report listing each edge case checked and any required corrections to the proof candidate.
      </deliverable>
    </worker>
  </workers>

  <orchestration>
    Collect all three worker reports. If counterexample_hunter or boundary_auditor identifies a defect, request a revised constructive proof. Only after all three reports agree and the proof is complete and self-contained will the final proof be submitted as a candidate to the outer audit gate.
  </orchestration>
</MRA_ACTION>
